# FILE: /Users/bluephoenix/frappe-bench/bench-r2/apps/frappe_flowbridge/benchmarks/k6/load_test.js
// k6 realistic load test — Phase 18-G (18.37)
// Usage: k6 run --env SLUG=my-endpoint --env TOKEN=xxx load_test.js
// Thresholds gate deployment: p99 < 50ms, error rate < 1%.

import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Counter, Rate, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const SLUG  = __ENV.SLUG  || "test-endpoint";
const TOKEN = __ENV.TOKEN || "test-token";
const BASE  = __ENV.BASE  || "http://localhost:8080";

const errorRate    = new Rate("errors");
const getLatency   = new Trend("get_latency_ms", true);
const writeLatency = new Trend("write_latency_ms", true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    // 500 VUs, 80% GET / 15% POST / 5% PATCH — Phase 18.37
    realistic: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      startVUs: 0,
      stages: [
        { duration: "30s", target: 100 },
        { duration: "2m",  target: 500 },
        { duration: "30s", target: 0   },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    // Deployment gate — CI fails if these are breached
    "http_req_duration{scenario:realistic}": ["p(99)<50"],
    errors: ["rate<0.01"],
    get_latency_ms: ["p(95)<20", "p(99)<50"],
    write_latency_ms: ["p(95)<200", "p(99)<500"],
  },
};

const headers = {
  Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`,
  "Content-Type": "application/json",
};

export default function () {
  const roll = Math.random();

  if (roll < 0.80) {
    // GET list
    const t0  = Date.now();
    const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/v1/${SLUG}?limit=20`, { headers });
    getLatency.add(Date.now() - t0);
    const ok = check(res, {
      "GET 200": (r) => r.status === 200,
      "GET has data": (r) => {
        try { return Array.isArray(JSON.parse(r.body).data); } catch { return false; }
      },
    });
    errorRate.add(!ok);

  } else if (roll < 0.95) {
    // POST create
    const t0  = Date.now();
    const res = http.post(
      `${BASE}/api/v1/${SLUG}`,
      JSON.stringify({ name: `K6-${__VU}-${__ITER}`, value: __ITER }),
      { headers },
    );
    writeLatency.add(Date.now() - t0);
    const ok = check(res, {
      "POST 200/201/202": (r) => [200, 201, 202].includes(r.status),
    });
    errorRate.add(!ok);

  } else {
    // PATCH update
    const t0  = Date.now();
    const res = http.patch(
      `${BASE}/api/v1/${SLUG}?name=K6-${__VU}-1`,
      JSON.stringify({ value: __ITER }),
      { headers },
    );
    writeLatency.add(Date.now() - t0);
    const ok = check(res, {
      "PATCH 200/202": (r) => [200, 202].includes(r.status),
    });
    errorRate.add(!ok);
  }

  sleep(0.01); // 10ms think time
}

# FILE: /Users/bluephoenix/frappe-bench/bench-r2/apps/frappe_flowbridge/frappe_flowbridge/flowbridge/api/agents.py
"""
FlowBridge ERPNext AI Agents — Phase 3.3, 3.3a–c, AI-4.2, AI-4.3
Tool-using agent framework where Claude (or any LLM) can call ERPNext APIs
to answer questions, perform actions, and retrieve data.

Agents are grounded on real-time ERPNext data fetched via Frappe's ORM.
RAG (3.3a) retrieves relevant documents before each agent response.
Vector store (3.3b) indexes ERPNext items/customers/orders.
Chatbot (3.3c) exposes a conversational interface for internal/customer use.
"""
import json
import frappe
from frappe import _


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool definitions (Claude tool_use format)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

AGENT_TOOLS = [
	{
		"name": "search_documents",
		"description": "Search ERPNext documents by keyword across a DocType.",
		"input_schema": {
			"type": "object",
			"properties": {
				"doctype": {"type": "string", "description": "E.g. 'Customer', 'Item', 'Sales Order'"},
				"query": {"type": "string", "description": "Search keyword"},
				"limit": {"type": "integer", "default": 5},
			},
			"required": ["doctype", "query"],
		},
	},
	{
		"name": "get_document",
		"description": "Fetch a specific ERPNext document by DocType and name.",
		"input_schema": {
			"type": "object",
			"properties": {
				"doctype": {"type": "string"},
				"name": {"type": "string"},
				"fields": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"},
				           "description": "Fields to return. Empty = all."},
			},
			"required": ["doctype", "name"],
		},
	},
	{
		"name": "create_document",
		"description": "Create a new ERPNext document.",
		"input_schema": {
			"type": "object",
			"properties": {
				"doctype": {"type": "string"},
				"values": {"type": "object", "description": "Field values for the new document."},
			},
			"required": ["doctype", "values"],
		},
	},
	{
		"name": "run_sql",
		"description": "Run a read-only SQL query on the ERPNext database (SELECT only).",
		"input_schema": {

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool executor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _execute_tool(tool_name: str, tool_input: dict, user: str) -> str:
	"""Execute a tool call and return a string result."""
	try:
		if tool_name == "search_documents":
			return _tool_search(tool_input)
		elif tool_name == "get_document":
			return _tool_get(tool_input)
		elif tool_name == "create_document":
			return _tool_create(tool_input, user)
		elif tool_name == "run_sql":
			return _tool_sql(tool_input)
		elif tool_name == "run_flow":
			return _tool_run_flow(tool_input)
		elif tool_name == "retrieve_context":
			return _tool_rag(tool_input)
		else:
			return f"Unknown tool: {tool_name}"
	except Exception as e:
		return f"Tool error: {str(e)[:300]}"


def _tool_search(inp: dict) -> str:
	doctype = inp["doctype"]
	query = inp["query"]
	limit = min(int(inp.get("limit", 5)), 20)
	try:
		results = frappe.get_all(
			doctype,
			filters=[["name", "like", f"%{query}%"]],
			fields=["name", "creation"],
			limit=limit,
		)
		if not results:
			# Try OR search on common text fields
			common = frappe.get_meta(doctype).get_search_fields()
			or_filters = [[doctype, f, "like", f"%{query}%"] for f in (common or ["name"])[:3]]
			results = frappe.get_all(doctype, or_filters=or_filters, limit=limit)
		return json.dumps(results[:limit], default=str)
	except Exception as e:
		return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})


def _tool_get(inp: dict) -> str:
	doctype = inp["doctype"]
	name = inp["name"]
	fields = inp.get("fields") or []
	try:
		doc = frappe.get_doc(doctype, name)
		if fields:
			data = {f: doc.get(f) for f in fields if hasattr(doc, f)}
		else:
			data = doc.as_dict()
			# Truncate large fields
			for k, v in list(data.items()):
				if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > 500:
					data[k] = v[:500] + "…"
		return json.dumps(data, default=str)[:3000]
	except Exception as e:
		return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})


def _tool_create(inp: dict, user: str) -> str:
	doctype = inp["doctype"]
	values = inp.get("values", {})
	# Safety: only allow specific doctypes for agent creation
	ALLOWED_DOCTYPES = {"Customer", "Supplier", "Item", "Sales Order", "Lead",
	                    "Contact", "Address", "Journal Entry", "FB Flow Run"}
	if doctype not in ALLOWED_DOCTYPES:
		return json.dumps({"error": f"DocType '{doctype}' is not allowed for agent creation."})
	try:
		doc = frappe.new_doc(doctype)
		doc.update(values)
		doc.flags.ignore_permissions = True
		doc.insert(ignore_permissions=True)
		frappe.db.commit()
		return json.dumps({"name": doc.name, "doctype": doctype, "created": True})
	except Exception as e:
		return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})


def _tool_sql(inp: dict) -> str:
	sql = inp["sql"].strip()
	# Safety: only allow SELECT
	if not sql.upper().lstrip().startswith("SELECT"):
		return json.dumps({"error": "Only SELECT queries are allowed."})
	try:
		result = frappe.db.sql(sql, as_dict=True)
		return json.dumps(result[:50], default=str)[:3000]
	except Exception as e:
		return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})


def _tool_run_flow(inp: dict) -> str:
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.executor.runner import enqueue_flow_run
	try:
		run_name = enqueue_flow_run(inp["flow_name"], inp.get("payload", {}), trigger="agent")
		return json.dumps({"run_name": run_name, "status": "queued"})
	except Exception as e:
		return json.dumps({"error": str(e)})


def _tool_rag(inp: dict) -> str:
	"""AI-3.3a: Retrieve relevant ERPNext data as RAG context."""
	question = inp["question"]
	doc_types = inp.get("doc_types") or ["Item", "Customer", "Sales Order"]
	results = []
	for dt in doc_types[:3]:
		try:
			rows = frappe.get_all(dt, limit=5, fields=["name", "creation"])
			for row in rows[:3]:
				results.append({"doctype": dt, "name": row.name})
		except Exception:
			pass
	# Also search via vector index if available
	try:
		from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.default_engine import erpnext_faq
		faq_hits = erpnext_faq(question, top_k=2)
		for hit in faq_hits:
			results.append({"topic": hit["topic"], "answer": hit["answer"]})
	except Exception:
		pass
	return json.dumps(results, default=str)[:2000]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent runner — multi-turn tool loop (3.3, AI-4.2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def run_agent(question: str, context: dict = None, max_turns: int = 5,
              user: str = None) -> dict:
	"""
	Run an ERPNext-grounded AI agent.
	Returns {"answer": str, "tool_calls": list, "turns": int}.
	"""
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine
	engine = get_engine("agent")

	# For non-Claude providers, fall back to simple RAG + completion
	if not hasattr(engine, "_api_key") or not hasattr(engine, "_model"):
		return _simple_agent(question, engine, context)

	# Claude-style multi-turn tool loop
	try:
		import anthropic
		client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=engine._api_key)
	except Exception:
		return _simple_agent(question, engine, context)

	system = _agent_system_prompt(context)
	messages = [{"role": "user", "content": question}]
	tool_calls_log = []
	current_user = user or frappe.session.user

	for turn in range(max_turns):
		resp = client.messages.create(
			model=engine._model,
			max_tokens=2048,
			system=system,
			tools=AGENT_TOOLS,
			messages=messages,
		)

		# Collect any text + tool_use blocks
		answer_parts = []
		tool_uses = []
		for block in resp.content:
			if block.type == "text":
				answer_parts.append(block.text)
			elif block.type == "tool_use":
				tool_uses.append(block)

		if resp.stop_reason == "end_turn" or not tool_uses:
			return {
				"answer": " ".join(answer_parts).strip(),
				"tool_calls": tool_calls_log,
				"turns": turn + 1,
				"provider": engine.name,
			}

		# Execute tool calls and continue conversation
		messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": resp.content})
		tool_results = []
		for tu in tool_uses:
			result = _execute_tool(tu.name, tu.input, current_user)
			tool_calls_log.append({"tool": tu.name, "input": tu.input, "result": result[:200]})
			tool_results.append({
				"type": "tool_result",
				"tool_use_id": tu.id,
				"content": result,
			})
		messages.append({"role": "user", "content": tool_results})

	return {"answer": "Agent reached max turns without a final answer.", "tool_calls": tool_calls_log, "turns": max_turns}


def _simple_agent(question: str, engine, context: dict) -> dict:
	"""Fallback: single-shot RAG + LLM completion for non-Claude providers."""
	rag = _tool_rag({"question": question})
	system = _agent_system_prompt(context) + f"\n\nRelevant ERPNext data:\n{rag}"
	answer = engine.complete(system, question)
	return {"answer": answer, "tool_calls": [], "turns": 1, "provider": engine.name}


def _agent_system_prompt(context: dict = None) -> str:
	ctx_str = ""
	if context:
		ctx_str = f"\n\nCurrent context:\n{json.dumps(context, default=str)[:500]}"

	return f"""You are an ERPNext AI Agent for FlowBridge.
You have access to tools to search, read, and create ERPNext documents, run SQL queries, and trigger FlowBridge flows.

Guidelines:
- Always use retrieve_context first to get relevant ERPNext data before answering.
- Use search_documents to find specific records.
- Never run destructive SQL — only SELECT queries.
- When creating documents, confirm the values with the user first (summarise what you're about to create).
- Prefer precise answers over long explanations.
- If you cannot find the data, say so clearly.
{ctx_str}"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Whitelisted endpoints
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def agent_chat(question: str, context_json: str = "{}", max_turns: int = 5) -> dict:
	"""3.3c: ERPNext-aware chatbot endpoint."""
	context = json.loads(context_json) if isinstance(context_json, str) else context_json
	return run_agent(question, context=context, max_turns=int(max_turns))


@frappe.whitelist()
def agent_rag_search(question: str, doc_types: str = "[]") -> list:
	"""3.3a/3.3b: RAG retrieval endpoint."""
	dts = json.loads(doc_types) if isinstance(doc_types, str) else doc_types
	result = json.loads(_tool_rag({"question": question, "doc_types": dts}))
	return result if isinstance(result, list) else [result]


@frappe.whitelist()
def build_vector_store(doc_types: str = '["Item","Customer","Sales Order"]') -> dict:
	"""
	3.3b: Index ERPNext documents into the vector store.
	Invalidates and rebuilds the connector + flow template indexes.
	"""
	frappe.only_for(["System Manager"])
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.vector_index import (
		get_connector_index, get_flow_template_index, invalidate_all
	)
	invalidate_all()
	ci = get_connector_index()
	fi = get_flow_template_index()
	dts = json.loads(doc_types) if isinstance(doc_types, str) else doc_types
	return {
		"connectors_indexed": len(ci._items),
		"flows_indexed": len(fi._items),
		"doc_types": dts,
		"status": "indexed",
	}

# FILE: /Users/bluephoenix/frappe-bench/bench-r2/apps/frappe_flowbridge/frappe_flowbridge/flowbridge/api/ai.py
"""
FlowBridge AI API — Phase 3
  3.1  — AI Flow Builder (NL → flowbridge/v1 JSON)
  3.17 — AI Connector Builder (NL → connector.json)
  3.8–3.13 — FlowBridge Copilot (error logs, analytics, flow designer, marketplace)
  3.18 — AI auto-map for connector request/response fields
"""
import frappe
import json


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.1 — AI Flow Builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def build_flow(description: str, install: bool = False) -> dict:
	"""
	Generate a flowbridge/v1 Flow JSON from a natural language description.

	Args:
		description: Plain English description of what the flow should do.
		install: If True, immediately import the generated flow as a Draft.

	Returns:
		{"flow_json": {...}, "installed": bool, "flow_name": str, "provider": str}
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine

	engine = get_engine("flow_builder")
	connectors = _get_connector_summary()
	node_types = _node_type_reference()

	system = f"""You are FlowBridge's AI Flow Builder. Generate flowbridge/v1 JSON flows.

CONNECTOR LIBRARY (available connectors and their endpoints):
{json.dumps(connectors, indent=2)}

NODE TYPES:
{node_types}

RULES:
1. Output ONLY valid JSON — no markdown fences, no explanation outside JSON.
2. The root object must have: schema="flowbridge/v1", type="Flow", name (slug), trigger_type, nodes[], settings.
3. Every node needs: node_id (unique slug), node_type, node_name, config_json (dict), on_error.
4. Routing: set next_node_id for linear flow; true_next_node_id/false_next_node_id for condition nodes.
5. Use retry_count + retry_delay_seconds for nodes calling external APIs (on_error: retry).
6. Use dlq_enabled: 1 in settings for critical flows.
7. node_type values: webhook_trigger, schedule_trigger, doctype_trigger, http_request, action, transform, condition, create_doc, update_doc, delete_doc, notify, delay, loop, sub_flow.
8. For condition nodes, config_json.expression is a Jinja2 boolean expression.
9. For create_doc/update_doc, config_json.fields contains Jinja2-templated field values.
10. For notify, config_json.channel: email | frappe_notification | webhook.

Return exactly one JSON object."""

	user = f"Build a FlowBridge flow for: {description}"

	raw = engine.complete(system, user, max_tokens=4096)
	provider = engine.name

	# Parse and validate
	flow_json = _extract_json(raw)
	if not flow_json:
		return {"error": "AI returned invalid JSON", "raw": raw[:500], "provider": provider}

	_ensure_flow_schema(flow_json)

	result = {"flow_json": flow_json, "installed": False, "flow_name": flow_json.get("name", ""), "provider": provider}

	if install and flow_json.get("name"):
		try:
			from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.api.flow import import_flow
			import_flow(flow_json, overwrite=False)
			result["installed"] = True
		except Exception as e:
			result["install_error"] = str(e)

	return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.17 — AI Connector Builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def build_connector(
	description: str,
	base_url: str = "",
	example_request: str = "",
	example_response: str = "",
	install: bool = False,
) -> dict:
	"""
	Generate an FB Connector + Endpoints from a plain English description.

	Returns:
		{"connector_json": {...}, "installed": bool, "connector_name": str}
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine

	engine = get_engine("connector_builder")

	system = """You are FlowBridge's AI Connector Builder.

Generate a JSON document describing a FlowBridge connector. Schema:
{
  "connector_name": "string (slug, e.g. 'my-api')",
  "display_name": "string",
  "base_url": "string",
  "auth_type": "none | api_key | bearer | basic | oauth2_client_credentials | hmac",
  "description": "string",
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "endpoint_name": "string (slug)",
      "display_name": "string",
      "method": "GET | POST | PUT | PATCH | DELETE",
      "path": "string (e.g. /orders/{order_id})",
      "description": "string",
      "request_body_format": "json | form | none",
      "response_format": "json | xml | auto",
      "response_root_path": "string (dot-notation path to data array/object)",
      "parameters": [
        {"name": "string", "type": "path | query | body | header", "required": true, "description": "string"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

RULES:
1. Output ONLY valid JSON. No markdown, no explanation.
2. Generate 3–10 meaningful endpoints covering the main CRUD operations.
3. Use {param_name} in path for path parameters.
4. For auth_type api_key, the key goes in a header named X-API-Key by convention.
5. response_root_path: the JSON path to the list/object in the response (e.g. "data", "results.items").
6. If base_url not provided, infer from the description or use a placeholder."""

	user_parts = [f"Build a connector for: {description}"]
	if base_url:
		user_parts.append(f"Base URL: {base_url}")
	if example_request:
		user_parts.append(f"Example request:\n{example_request}")
	if example_response:
		user_parts.append(f"Example response:\n{example_response}")

	raw = engine.complete(system, "\n\n".join(user_parts), max_tokens=4096)
	provider = engine.name

	connector_json = _extract_json(raw)
	if not connector_json:
		return {"error": "AI returned invalid JSON", "raw": raw[:500], "provider": provider}

	result = {
		"connector_json": connector_json,
		"installed": False,
		"connector_name": connector_json.get("connector_name", ""),
		"provider": provider,
	}

	if install and connector_json.get("connector_name"):
		try:
			_install_connector(connector_json)
			result["installed"] = True
		except Exception as e:
			result["install_error"] = str(e)

	return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.18 — AI auto-map connector fields
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def automap_connector_fields(
	connector_name: str,
	endpoint_name: str,
	target_doctype: str,
	sample_response: str = "",
) -> dict:
	"""
	Given a connector endpoint and target DocType, suggest field mappings.
	Uses AI to reason about semantic equivalence when pure synonym matching fails.
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.field_mapper_ai import suggest_mappings

	# Get source fields from connector endpoint response schema or sample
	source_fields = []
	if sample_response:
		try:
			sample = json.loads(sample_response)
			source_fields = _flatten_keys(sample)
		except json.JSONDecodeError:
			pass

	if not source_fields:
		# Try fetching from connector config
		try:
			ep_doc = frappe.get_doc("FB Connector Endpoint",
				{"connector": connector_name, "endpoint_name": endpoint_name})
			if ep_doc.mock_response_json:
				sample = json.loads(ep_doc.mock_response_json)
				source_fields = _flatten_keys(sample)
		except Exception:
			pass

	# Target fields from DocType meta
	meta = frappe.get_meta(target_doctype)
	skip_types = {"Section Break", "Column Break", "HTML", "Heading", "Button", "Fold", "Tab Break"}
	skip_fields = {"name", "owner", "creation", "modified", "modified_by", "docstatus",
	               "parent", "parentfield", "parenttype", "idx", "doctype"}
	target_fields = [
		f.fieldname for f in meta.fields
		if f.fieldtype not in skip_types and f.fieldname not in skip_fields
	]

	# Start with heuristic mapper
	heuristic = suggest_mappings(source_fields, target_fields, top_n=3, min_score=0.4)

	# For low-confidence mappings, ask AI
	low_confidence = [
		tgt for tgt, suggestions in heuristic.items()
		if not suggestions or (suggestions and suggestions[0]["score"] < 0.65)
	]

	ai_mappings = {}
	if low_confidence and source_fields:
		engine = get_engine("field_mapper")
		system = (
			"You are a field mapping assistant. Given source API fields and target DocType fields, "
			"output a JSON object mapping target_field → source_field for the best semantic match. "
			"Only include pairs where you are confident. Output ONLY JSON."
		)
		user = (
			f"Source fields: {json.dumps(source_fields[:50])}\n"
			f"Target fields needing mapping: {json.dumps(low_confidence[:30])}\n"
			f"Target DocType: {target_doctype}\n"
			"Return JSON: {{target_field: source_field, ...}}"
		)
		raw = engine.complete(system, user, max_tokens=1024)
		ai_raw = _extract_json(raw)
		if isinstance(ai_raw, dict):
			ai_mappings = ai_raw

	# Also use vector similarity mapper (AI-3.1) for low-confidence targets
	if low_confidence:
		try:
			from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.default_engine import suggest_field_mappings
			vector_suggestions = suggest_field_mappings(source_fields, low_confidence, threshold=0.3)
			for sug in vector_suggestions:
				if sug["target"] not in ai_mappings:
					ai_mappings[sug["target"]] = sug["source"]
		except Exception:
			pass

	# Merge: heuristic takes precedence, then AI, then vector
	merged = {}
	for tgt in target_fields:
		if tgt in heuristic and heuristic[tgt]:
			merged[tgt] = {"source": heuristic[tgt][0]["field"], "score": heuristic[tgt][0]["score"], "method": "heuristic"}
		elif tgt in ai_mappings:
			merged[tgt] = {"source": ai_mappings[tgt], "score": 0.5, "method": "ai"}

	return {
		"connector": connector_name,
		"endpoint": endpoint_name,
		"target_doctype": target_doctype,
		"mappings": merged,
		"source_fields": source_fields,
		"unmapped_targets": [t for t in target_fields if t not in merged],
	}

@frappe.whitelist()
def copilot_explain_error(run_name: str) -> dict:
	"""3.10 — Explain a failed flow run in plain English and suggest fixes."""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine

	run = frappe.get_doc("FB Flow Run", run_name)
	failed_steps = [s for s in run.steps if s.status == "Failed"]

	if not failed_steps:
		return {"explanation": "No failed steps found in this run.", "suggestions": []}

	context = {
		"flow": run.flow,
		"trigger": run.trigger,
		"error_message": run.error_message,
		"failed_steps": [
			{
				"node_id": s.node_id,
				"node_type": s.node_type,
				"error": s.error_message,
				"input": s.input_json[:500] if s.input_json else "",
			}
			for s in failed_steps[:5]
		],
	}

	engine = get_engine("error_explainer")
	system = (
		"You are a FlowBridge integration expert. Analyse flow run failures and provide:\n"
		"1. A plain-English explanation of what went wrong (2–3 sentences)\n"
		"2. A numbered list of concrete fix suggestions\n"
		"3. Whether this is transient (retry) or requires config change\n"
		"Format as JSON: {explanation, suggestions: [str], is_transient: bool}"
	)
	user = f"Flow run failure context:\n{json.dumps(context, indent=2, default=str)}"

	# Default Engine: use rule-based error categorizer if no LLM (AI-3.4)
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.default_engine import categorize_error
	first_error = failed_steps[0].error_message or run.error_message or ""
	default_cat = categorize_error(first_error)

	if hasattr(engine, "_api_key") or hasattr(engine, "_base_url"):
		raw = engine.complete(system, user, max_tokens=1024)
		result = _extract_json(raw)
		if not result:
			result = {"explanation": raw, "suggestions": [], "is_transient": default_cat["is_transient"]}
	else:
		result = {
			"explanation": f"[Default Engine] {default_cat['suggestion']}",
			"suggestions": [default_cat["suggestion"]],
			"is_transient": default_cat["is_transient"],
			"category": default_cat["category"],
		}

	result["provider"] = engine.name
	result["run_name"] = run_name
	return result

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _extract_json(text: str) -> dict | list | None:
	"""Extract the first valid JSON object or array from a text response."""
	if not text:
		return None
	# Strip markdown fences
	import re
	text = re.sub(r"```(?:json)?\s*", "", text).strip()
	text = text.rstrip("`").strip()
	# Try direct parse
	try:
		return json.loads(text)
	except json.JSONDecodeError:
		pass
	# Find first { or [
	for start_char, end_char in [('{', '}'), ('[', ']')]:
		start = text.find(start_char)
		if start == -1:
			continue
		# Find matching closing bracket
		depth = 0
		for i, ch in enumerate(text[start:], start):
			if ch == start_char:
				depth += 1
			elif ch == end_char:
				depth -= 1
				if depth == 0:
					try:
						return json.loads(text[start:i + 1])
					except json.JSONDecodeError:
						break
	return None


def _ensure_flow_schema(flow_json: dict):
	"""Fill in defaults so the flow JSON is always valid for import."""
	flow_json.setdefault("schema", "flowbridge/v1")
	flow_json.setdefault("type", "Flow")
	flow_json.setdefault("trigger_type", "Manual")
	flow_json.setdefault("nodes", [])
	flow_json.setdefault("settings", {
		"max_concurrent_runs": 5,
		"timeout_seconds": 300,
		"dlq_enabled": 0,
	})
	if not flow_json.get("name"):
		import re
		flow_json["name"] = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9-]", "-",
			flow_json.get("trigger_type", "flow").lower())[:40]


def _get_connector_summary() -> list:
	"""Return a condensed summary of all connectors and their endpoints."""
	connectors = frappe.get_all("FB Connector",
		fields=["connector_name", "base_url", "auth_type"],
		limit=30,
	)
	result = []
	for conn in connectors:
		endpoints = frappe.get_all("FB Connector Endpoint",
			filters={"connector": conn.connector_name},
			fields=["endpoint_name", "method", "path", "description"],
			limit=10,
		)
		result.append({
			"name": conn.connector_name,
			"base_url": conn.base_url,
			"auth": conn.auth_type,
			"endpoints": [{"name": e.endpoint_name, "method": e.method, "path": e.path} for e in endpoints],
		})
	return result


def _node_type_reference() -> str:
	return """Node types and their config_json fields:
- webhook_trigger: {} (no config needed)
- schedule_trigger: {cron: "* * * * *"}
- doctype_trigger: {doctype: "DocType Name", event: "after_insert|on_update|on_submit|on_cancel"}
- http_request/action: connector (field), endpoint (field), config_json for extra params
- condition: {expression: "Jinja2 boolean, e.g. payload.status == 'active'"}
- transform: {rules: [{source: "path", target: "field", transform: "transform_name"}]}
- create_doc: {doctype: "Name", fields: {field: "{{ Jinja2 template }}"}}
- update_doc: {doctype: "Name", name_template: "{{ expr }}", fields: {field: "value"}}
- delete_doc: {doctype: "Name", name: "{{ expr }}"}
- notify: {channel: "email|frappe_notification|webhook", message: "{{ Jinja2 }}", recipients: ["email"]}
- delay: {seconds: 30}
- loop: {items_key: "ctx_key", child_flow: "flow-name", max_items: 100}
- sub_flow: {flow: "flow-name", pass_keys: ["key1", "key2"]}"""


def _flatten_keys(obj, prefix: str = "", depth: int = 3) -> list:
	"""Recursively extract dot-notation keys from a JSON object."""
	keys = []
	if depth <= 0 or not isinstance(obj, dict):
		return keys
	for k, v in obj.items():
		full = f"{prefix}.{k}" if prefix else k
		keys.append(full)
		if isinstance(v, dict):
			keys.extend(_flatten_keys(v, full, depth - 1))
		elif isinstance(v, list) and v and isinstance(v[0], dict):
			keys.extend(_flatten_keys(v[0], f"{full}[*]", depth - 1))
	return keys


def _install_connector(data: dict):
	"""Create FB Connector + FB Connector Endpoint records from AI-generated JSON."""
	name = data["connector_name"]
	if not frappe.db.exists("FB Connector", name):
		conn = frappe.get_doc({
			"doctype": "FB Connector",
			"connector_name": name,
			"base_url": data.get("base_url", ""),
			"auth_type": data.get("auth_type", "none"),
			"description": data.get("description", ""),
		})
		conn.insert(ignore_permissions=True)

	for ep in data.get("endpoints", []):
		ep_name = f"{name}-{ep.get('endpoint_name', 'endpoint')}"
		if not frappe.db.exists("FB Connector Endpoint", ep_name):
			frappe.get_doc({
				"doctype": "FB Connector Endpoint",
				"name": ep_name,
				"connector": name,
				"endpoint_name": ep.get("endpoint_name", ""),
				"method": ep.get("method", "GET"),
				"path": ep.get("path", "/"),
				"description": ep.get("description", ""),
				"request_body_format": ep.get("request_body_format", "json"),
				"response_format": ep.get("response_format", "json"),
				"response_root_path": ep.get("response_root_path", ""),
			}).insert(ignore_permissions=True)

	frappe.db.commit()


def _default_next_nodes(current_type: str) -> list:
	"""Rule-based fallback suggestions when no AI provider is configured."""
	suggestions_map = {
		"webhook_trigger": [
			{"node_type": "condition", "node_name": "Validate Payload", "reason": "Validate the webhook payload before processing", "config_hint": '{"expression": "payload.event is defined"}'},
			{"node_type": "transform", "node_name": "Map Fields", "reason": "Map webhook fields to ERPNext fields", "config_hint": "{}"},
			{"node_type": "http_request", "node_name": "Call API", "reason": "Make an API call with the webhook data", "config_hint": "{}"},
		],
		"condition": [
			{"node_type": "create_doc", "node_name": "Create Record", "reason": "True branch: create an ERPNext document", "config_hint": '{"doctype": "Sales Order"}'},
			{"node_type": "notify", "node_name": "Send Notification", "reason": "False branch: alert the team", "config_hint": '{"channel": "frappe_notification"}'},
			{"node_type": "http_request", "node_name": "Call External API", "reason": "Make a conditional API call", "config_hint": "{}"},
		],
		"http_request": [
			{"node_type": "condition", "node_name": "Check Response", "reason": "Branch on API response status", "config_hint": '{"expression": "http_response.status == 200"}'},
			{"node_type": "create_doc", "node_name": "Create ERPNext Record", "reason": "Store API response as ERPNext document", "config_hint": "{}"},
			{"node_type": "transform", "node_name": "Transform Response", "reason": "Map API response to target fields", "config_hint": "{}"},
		],
	}
	return suggestions_map.get(current_type, [
		{"node_type": "notify", "node_name": "Notify", "reason": "Send a notification", "config_hint": '{"channel": "frappe_notification"}'},
		{"node_type": "condition", "node_name": "Check Condition", "reason": "Add conditional logic", "config_hint": "{}"},
		{"node_type": "delay", "node_name": "Add Delay", "reason": "Wait before next step", "config_hint": '{"seconds": 30}'},
	])

# AI-4.4: Full contextual Copilot — multi-turn with history
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def contextual_copilot(messages: str, flow_name: str = "", connector_name: str = "") -> dict:
	"""
	AI-4.4: Full contextual Copilot with conversation history.
	messages: JSON array of {role, content} objects.
	"""
	from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine
	msgs = json.loads(messages) if isinstance(messages, str) else messages

	engine = get_engine("copilot")
	context_parts = ["You are FlowBridge Copilot — an expert integration assistant."]
	if flow_name and frappe.db.exists("FB Flow", flow_name):
		flow = frappe.get_doc("FB Flow", flow_name)
		context_parts.append(f"Current flow: {flow.flow_name} ({flow.trigger_type}, {len(flow.nodes)} nodes).")
	if connector_name and frappe.db.exists("FB Connector", connector_name):
		conn = frappe.get_doc("FB Connector", connector_name)
		context_parts.append(f"Current connector: {conn.connector_name} ({conn.base_url}).")

	system = " ".join(context_parts)

	# Build conversation string for non-multi-turn providers
	conversation = "\n".join(f"{m['role'].upper()}: {m['content']}" for m in msgs[-8:])
	user_msg = msgs[-1]["content"] if msgs else ""

	# Try multi-turn for Claude
	try:
		import anthropic
		if hasattr(engine, "_api_key"):
			client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=engine._api_key)
			resp = client.messages.create(
				model=engine._model, max_tokens=1024, system=system, messages=msgs[-10:]
			)
			return {"reply": resp.content[0].text, "provider": engine.name}
	except Exception:
		pass

	reply = engine.complete(system, conversation)
	return {"reply": reply, "provider": engine.name}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AI-4.5: NL → flow JSON (advanced, with prompt library lookup)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def build_flow_advanced(description: str, install: bool = False,
                        prompt_name: str = "") -> dict:
	"""
	AI-4.5: Advanced flow builder — uses custom prompt from library if configured.
	Falls back to standard build_flow() if no custom prompt exists.
	"""
	if prompt_name:
		try:
			from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.api.prompt_library import get_active_prompt, render_prompt
			from frappe_flowbridge.flowbridge.utils.ai_engine import get_engine
			prompt = get_active_prompt("flow_builder", prompt_name)
			if prompt:
				system, user = render_prompt(prompt, {"description": description})
				engine = get_engine("flow_builder")
				raw = engine.complete(system, user or description)
				flow_json = _extract_json(raw)
				if flow_json:
					_ensure_flow_schema(flow_json)
					return {"flow_json": flow_json, "provider": engine.name, "prompt_used": prompt_name}
		except Exception:
			pass

	return build_flow(description, install=install)

# FILE: /Users/bluephoenix/frappe-bench/bench-r2/apps/frappe_flowbridge/frappe_flowbridge/flowbridge/api/analytics.py
"""
FlowBridge Analytics API — Phase 3 (3.5, 3.6, 3.7)
  3.5 — Advanced per-flow analytics (node timing, percentiles, trend)
  3.6 — Cross-flow analytics & anomaly detection (IsolationForest)
  3.7 — Predictive failure detection (trend-based)
"""
import frappe
import json
import math
import statistics
from frappe.utils import now_datetime, add_days


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.5 — Advanced per-flow analytics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def get_flow_analytics(flow_name: str, days: int = 30) -> dict:
	"""
	Per-flow deep analytics: node timing, error rate per node,
	P50/P95/P99 latency, daily trend, success rate.
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	days = int(days)
	since = add_days(now_datetime(), -days)

	runs = frappe.get_all("FB Flow Run",
		filters={"flow": flow_name, "started_at": [">=", since]},
		fields=["name", "status", "started_at", "ended_at", "duration_ms", "trigger"],
		order_by="started_at asc",
		limit=5000,
	)

	if not runs:
		return {"flow": flow_name, "days": days, "runs": 0, "no_data": True}

	total = len(runs)
	success = sum(1 for r in runs if r.status == "Success")
	failed = sum(1 for r in runs if r.status == "Failed")
	durations = [r.duration_ms for r in runs if r.duration_ms]

	# Percentiles
	percentiles = {}
	if durations:
		sorted_d = sorted(durations)
		percentiles = {
			"p50": _percentile(sorted_d, 50),
			"p95": _percentile(sorted_d, 95),
			"p99": _percentile(sorted_d, 99),
			"min": sorted_d[0],
			"max": sorted_d[-1],
			"avg": round(statistics.mean(durations), 1),
		}

	# Daily trend
	trend = _daily_trend(runs, days)

	# Per-node stats from steps
	node_stats = _node_stats(flow_name, since)

	# Error breakdown by trigger
	trigger_errors = {}
	for r in runs:
		if r.status == "Failed":
			t = r.trigger or "unknown"
			trigger_errors[t] = trigger_errors.get(t, 0) + 1

	return {
		"flow": flow_name,
		"days": days,
		"runs": total,
		"success": success,
		"failed": failed,
		"success_rate": round(success / total * 100, 1) if total else 0,
		"percentiles_ms": percentiles,
		"trend": trend,
		"node_stats": node_stats,
		"trigger_errors": trigger_errors,
	}


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_node_flame(flow_name: str, run_name: str = "") -> list:
	"""
	Return step-level timing for a specific run (flame chart data),
	or average timing per node across recent runs if run_name omitted.
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	if run_name:
		run = frappe.get_doc("FB Flow Run", run_name)
		return [
			{
				"node_id": s.node_id,
				"node_type": s.node_type,
				"status": s.status,
				"duration_ms": s.duration_ms or 0,
				"error": s.error_message,
			}
			for s in run.steps
		]
	return _node_stats(flow_name, add_days(now_datetime(), -7))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.6 — Cross-flow analytics & anomaly detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def get_cross_flow_summary(days: int = 7) -> list:
	"""
	Rank all active flows by volume, error rate, and avg duration.
	Flags anomalous flows using IsolationForest (scikit-learn) or
	a simple z-score fallback if scikit-learn is unavailable.
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	days = int(days)
	since = add_days(now_datetime(), -days)

	flows = frappe.get_all("FB Flow",
		filters={"status": "Active"},
		fields=["flow_name", "trigger_type"],
		limit=200,
	)

	summary = []
	for flow in flows:
		name = flow.flow_name
		runs = frappe.get_all("FB Flow Run",
			filters={"flow": name, "started_at": [">=", since]},
			fields=["status", "duration_ms"],
			limit=5000,
		)
		if not runs:
			continue
		total = len(runs)
		failed = sum(1 for r in runs if r.status == "Failed")
		durations = [r.duration_ms for r in runs if r.duration_ms]
		summary.append({
			"flow": name,
			"trigger_type": flow.trigger_type,
			"total_runs": total,
			"failed_runs": failed,
			"error_rate": round(failed / total * 100, 1),
			"avg_duration_ms": round(statistics.mean(durations), 1) if durations else 0,
		})

	if not summary:
		return []

	# Anomaly detection
	summary = _detect_anomalies(summary)
	summary.sort(key=lambda x: x["error_rate"], reverse=True)
	return summary


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_error_heatmap(days: int = 30) -> list:
	"""
	Return a list of {hour_of_day, day_of_week, count} buckets for failed runs —
	useful for rendering a calendar heatmap of failure patterns.
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	since = add_days(now_datetime(), -int(days))
	rows = frappe.db.sql("""
		SELECT
			HOUR(started_at) AS hour_of_day,
			DAYOFWEEK(started_at) AS day_of_week,
			COUNT(*) AS count
		FROM `tabFB Flow Run`
		WHERE status = 'Failed'
		  AND started_at >= %s
		GROUP BY hour_of_day, day_of_week
		ORDER BY day_of_week, hour_of_day
	""", since, as_dict=True)
	return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.7 — Predictive failure detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@frappe.whitelist()
def predict_failures(days: int = 14) -> list:
	"""
	For each active flow, compute a failure trend score over rolling windows.
	Returns flows predicted to degrade, ranked by risk score (0–100).
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	days = int(days)
	since = add_days(now_datetime(), -days)

	flows = frappe.get_all("FB Flow",
		filters={"status": "Active"},
		fields=["flow_name"],
		limit=200,
	)

	predictions = []
	for flow in flows:
		name = flow.flow_name
		runs = frappe.get_all("FB Flow Run",
			filters={"flow": name, "started_at": [">=", since]},
			fields=["status", "started_at", "duration_ms"],
			order_by="started_at asc",
			limit=5000,
		)
		if len(runs) < 10:
			continue

		pred = _compute_failure_prediction(name, runs, days)
		if pred["risk_score"] > 10:  # only surface meaningful risk
			predictions.append(pred)

	predictions.sort(key=lambda x: x["risk_score"], reverse=True)
	return predictions


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_flow_health_score(flow_name: str) -> dict:
	"""
	Compute a single 0–100 health score for a flow based on
	error rate, latency trend, and run volume consistency.
	"""
	frappe.only_for("System Manager")
	since = add_days(now_datetime(), -7)
	runs = frappe.get_all("FB Flow Run",
		filters={"flow": flow_name, "started_at": [">=", since]},
		fields=["status", "duration_ms", "started_at"],
		limit=5000,
	)
	if not runs:
		return {"flow": flow_name, "score": 100, "grade": "A", "reason": "No runs in last 7 days"}

	total = len(runs)
	failed = sum(1 for r in runs if r.status == "Failed")
	error_rate = failed / total
	durations = [r.duration_ms for r in runs if r.duration_ms]
	avg_ms = statistics.mean(durations) if durations else 0

	# Penalty components
	error_penalty = min(60, error_rate * 100)
	latency_penalty = min(20, max(0, (avg_ms - 500) / 100))  # >500ms starts costing
	volume_penalty = 5 if total < 3 else 0

	score = max(0, round(100 - error_penalty - latency_penalty - volume_penalty))
	grade = "A" if score >= 90 else "B" if score >= 75 else "C" if score >= 60 else "D" if score >= 40 else "F"

	return {
		"flow": flow_name,
		"score": score,
		"grade": grade,
		"error_rate_pct": round(error_rate * 100, 1),
		"avg_duration_ms": round(avg_ms, 1),
		"total_runs": total,
		"failed_runs": failed,
	}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _percentile(sorted_data: list, p: int) -> float:
	if not sorted_data:
		return 0
	k = (len(sorted_data) - 1) * p / 100
	f, c = math.floor(k), math.ceil(k)
	if f == c:
		return round(sorted_data[int(k)], 1)
	return round(sorted_data[f] * (c - k) + sorted_data[c] * (k - f), 1)


def _daily_trend(runs: list, days: int) -> list:
	"""Aggregate runs by day → list of {date, total, success, failed}."""
	from collections import defaultdict
	buckets: dict = defaultdict(lambda: {"total": 0, "success": 0, "failed": 0})
	for r in runs:
		day = str(r.started_at)[:10] if r.started_at else "unknown"
		buckets[day]["total"] += 1
		if r.status == "Success":
			buckets[day]["success"] += 1
		elif r.status == "Failed":
			buckets[day]["failed"] += 1
	return [{"date": d, **v} for d, v in sorted(buckets.items())]


def _node_stats(flow_name: str, since) -> list:
	"""Aggregate step durations and error rates per node_id."""
	rows = frappe.db.sql("""
		SELECT
			s.node_id,
			s.node_type,
			COUNT(*) AS executions,
			SUM(CASE WHEN s.status = 'Failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failures,
			AVG(s.duration_ms) AS avg_ms,
			MAX(s.duration_ms) AS max_ms
		FROM `tabFB Flow Run Step` s
		JOIN `tabFB Flow Run` r ON s.parent = r.name
		WHERE r.flow = %s AND r.started_at >= %s
		GROUP BY s.node_id, s.node_type
		ORDER BY avg_ms DESC
	""", (flow_name, since), as_dict=True)
	for row in rows:
		row["error_rate"] = round((row["failures"] / row["executions"]) * 100, 1) if row["executions"] else 0
		row["avg_ms"] = round(float(row["avg_ms"] or 0), 1)
		row["max_ms"] = round(float(row["max_ms"] or 0), 1)
	return rows


def _detect_anomalies(summary: list) -> list:
	"""
	Tag each flow as anomalous using IsolationForest (scikit-learn).
	Falls back to z-score if scikit-learn unavailable.
	"""
	for item in summary:
		item["is_anomaly"] = False
		item["anomaly_score"] = 0.0

	if len(summary) < 4:
		return summary

	try:
		from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
		import numpy as np

		X = np.array([
			[s["error_rate"], s["avg_duration_ms"], s["total_runs"]]
			for s in summary
		])
		clf = IsolationForest(contamination=0.15, random_state=42)
		labels = clf.fit_predict(X)
		scores = clf.score_samples(X)
		# Normalise scores to 0–100 (higher = more anomalous)
		s_min, s_max = scores.min(), scores.max()
		for i, item in enumerate(summary):
			item["is_anomaly"] = bool(labels[i] == -1)
			item["anomaly_score"] = round(
				(1 - (scores[i] - s_min) / (s_max - s_min + 1e-9)) * 100, 1
			)
	except ImportError:
		# z-score fallback
		rates = [s["error_rate"] for s in summary]
		if len(rates) > 1:
			mean = statistics.mean(rates)
			stdev = statistics.stdev(rates) or 1
			for item in summary:
				z = abs(item["error_rate"] - mean) / stdev
				item["is_anomaly"] = z > 2.0
				item["anomaly_score"] = round(min(100, z * 33), 1)

	return summary


def _compute_failure_prediction(flow_name: str, runs: list, days: int) -> dict:
	"""
	Split runs into first-half and second-half windows.
	Rising error rate + rising duration in second half = higher risk.
	"""
	half = len(runs) // 2
	first_half = runs[:half]
	second_half = runs[half:]

	def _error_rate(batch):
		if not batch:
			return 0
		return sum(1 for r in batch if r["status"] == "Failed") / len(batch)

	def _avg_ms(batch):
		ms = [r["duration_ms"] for r in batch if r.get("duration_ms")]
		return statistics.mean(ms) if ms else 0

	er_first = _error_rate(first_half)
	er_second = _error_rate(second_half)
	ms_first = _avg_ms(first_half)
	ms_second = _avg_ms(second_half)

	er_delta = er_second - er_first   # positive = worsening
	ms_delta = ms_second - ms_first   # positive = slower

	# Risk score: 0–100
	risk = min(100, round(
		max(0, er_delta) * 60 * 100          # error rate rise (weighted 60%)
		+ max(0, ms_delta / (ms_first + 1)) * 40 * 100  # latency rise (weighted 40%)
	))

	trend = "stable"
	if er_delta > 0.1:
		trend = "degrading"
	elif er_delta < -0.1:
		trend = "improving"

	return {
		"flow": flow_name,
		"risk_score": risk,
		"trend": trend,
		"error_rate_first_half": round(er_first * 100, 1),
		"error_rate_second_half": round(er_second * 100, 1),
		"avg_ms_first_half": round(ms_first, 1),
		"avg_ms_second_half": round(ms_second, 1),
		"total_runs": len(runs),
	}

# Phase 19 — AI-Native API Builder (19.1–19.15)

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import textwrap
from typing import Any

import frappe
from frappe import _

# ── helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _claude(messages: list[dict], system: str = "", max_tokens: int = 2048) -> str:
    """Call Claude API and return the assistant text content."""
    import anthropic
    client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=frappe.conf.get("anthropic_api_key", ""))
    kwargs: dict = dict(
        model="claude-opus-4-7",
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        messages=messages,
    )
    if system:
        kwargs["system"] = system
    response = client.messages.create(**kwargs)
    return response.content[0].text


def _endpoint_dict(cfg) -> dict:
    """Serialise a config object / doc to a plain dict for AI prompts."""
    if hasattr(cfg, "as_dict"):
        d = cfg.as_dict()
    else:
        d = dict(cfg)
    # Remove large blobs that don't add context
    for k in ("custom_logic", "mock_response", "__last_update"):
        d.pop(k, None)
    return d


def _load_cfg(slug: str):
    return frappe.get_doc("FB API Endpoint", slug)


# ── 19.1  NL → FB API Endpoint config ────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def build_endpoint_from_nl(prompt: str, base_slug: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """
    Translate a natural-language description into a draft FB API Endpoint config.
    Returns a dict that can be used to populate the DocType form.
    If base_slug is given the existing config is provided as context.
    """
    system = textwrap.dedent("""
        You are an expert at configuring FlowBridge API endpoints for Frappe/ERPNext.
        Given a natural-language description you produce a JSON object whose keys match
        FB API Endpoint fields.  Important fields:
          slug (str, kebab-case), label (str), primary_doctype (Link→DocType),
          allowed_methods (CSV: GET,POST,PATCH,DELETE), default_filters (JSON),
          fields (JSON list), enable_cache (0/1), cache_ttl_seconds (int),
          enable_auth (0/1), rate_limit_per_minute (int), enable_sse (0/1),
          null_policy (Keep|Omit|Empty String), custom_logic (python snippet or ""),
          description (str).
        Return ONLY valid JSON — no markdown fences, no extra text.
    """)
    context = ""
    if base_slug:
        try:
            context = "\n\nExisting config for context:\n" + json.dumps(
                _endpoint_dict(_load_cfg(base_slug)), indent=2
            )
        except Exception:
            pass

    reply = _claude(
        [{"role": "user", "content": prompt + context}],
        system=system,
        max_tokens=1024,
    )
    try:
        config = json.loads(reply)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        # Extract first JSON object if model wrapped it
        m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
        config = json.loads(m.group()) if m else {}
    return {"config": config, "source": "ai"}


# ── 19.2  Iterative refinement chat ──────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def refine_endpoint(slug: str, message: str, history: str = "[]") -> dict:
    """
    Continue a multi-turn conversation to iteratively refine an existing endpoint.
    `history` is a JSON array of {role, content} dicts from prior turns.
    Returns {reply, updated_config}.
    """
    cfg = _load_cfg(slug)
    prior: list[dict] = json.loads(history) if history else []

    system = textwrap.dedent(f"""
        You are refining the FlowBridge API endpoint "{slug}".
        Current config (JSON):
        {json.dumps(_endpoint_dict(cfg), indent=2)}

        When the user asks for a change, reply with a brief explanation followed by
        a JSON block delimited by ```json ... ``` containing only the fields to update.
        Keep unchanged fields out of the JSON block.
    """)
    messages = prior + [{"role": "user", "content": message}]
    reply = _claude(messages, system=system, max_tokens=1024)

    # Extract partial config from reply
    patch: dict = {}
    m = re.search(r"```json\s*(.*?)\s*```", reply, re.DOTALL)
    if m:
        try:
            patch = json.loads(m.group(1))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            pass

    return {"reply": reply, "patch": patch}


# ── 19.3  Config explanation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def explain_endpoint(slug: str) -> str:
    """Return a plain-English explanation of what this endpoint does."""
    cfg = _load_cfg(slug)
    system = "You explain FlowBridge API endpoint configurations concisely in plain English for non-technical stakeholders."
    prompt = (
        "Explain what the following API endpoint does, who should use it, "
        "what data it exposes, and any security/caching notes.\n\n"
        + json.dumps(_endpoint_dict(cfg), indent=2)
    )
    return _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=512)


# ── 19.4  Diff-aware update ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def apply_ai_patch(slug: str, patch: str) -> dict:
    """
    Apply a JSON patch dict (from refine_endpoint) to an existing endpoint.
    Saves the doc and returns {updated_fields, slug}.
    """
    patch_dict: dict = json.loads(patch) if isinstance(patch, str) else patch
    cfg = _load_cfg(slug)
    updated = []
    for key, val in patch_dict.items():
        if hasattr(cfg, key):
            setattr(cfg, key, val)
            updated.append(key)
    cfg.save(ignore_permissions=True)
    frappe.db.commit()
    return {"slug": slug, "updated_fields": updated}


# ── 19.5  Endpoint cloning + AI variation ────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def clone_with_variation(slug: str, variation_prompt: str) -> dict:
    """
    Clone an endpoint and apply an AI-generated variation described in plain English.
    Returns the new slug and draft config.
    """
    original = _load_cfg(slug)
    base_cfg = _endpoint_dict(original)

    system = textwrap.dedent("""
        You clone and vary FlowBridge API endpoint configs.
        Given the original config and a variation description, output a JSON object
        with the full new config. Change `slug` to be unique (append '-v2' or a short suffix).
        Return ONLY valid JSON.
    """)
    prompt = (
        f"Original config:\n{json.dumps(base_cfg, indent=2)}\n\n"
        f"Variation: {variation_prompt}"
    )
    reply = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=1024)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
    new_cfg: dict = json.loads(m.group()) if m else {}

    # Ensure slug is distinct
    new_slug = new_cfg.get("slug", slug + "-v2")
    if frappe.db.exists("FB API Endpoint", new_slug):
        new_slug = new_slug + "-" + hashlib.md5(variation_prompt.encode()).hexdigest()[:4]
        new_cfg["slug"] = new_slug

    return {"new_slug": new_slug, "config": new_cfg}

# ── 19.7  Semantic endpoint description embedding ────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def index_endpoint_embeddings() -> dict:
    """
    Generate semantic embeddings for all active endpoints and store them in Redis
    for similarity search (used by endpoint discovery).
    Returns {indexed: N}.
    """
    import anthropic
    r = frappe.cache()
    client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=frappe.conf.get("anthropic_api_key", ""))

    endpoints = frappe.get_all(
        "FB API Endpoint",
        filters={"is_active": 1},
        fields=["name", "label", "description", "primary_doctype"],
    )
    indexed = 0
    for ep in endpoints:
        text = f"{ep.label or ep.name}: {ep.description or ''} ({ep.primary_doctype})"
        resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input=text)
        vec = resp.data[0].embedding
        r.set(f"fb:emb:{ep.name}", json.dumps(vec), ex=86400)
        indexed += 1

    return {"indexed": indexed}


@frappe.whitelist()
def find_similar_endpoints(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> list[dict]:
    """
    Return the top-k endpoints semantically similar to the query string.
    Requires embeddings to be indexed first.
    """
    import math
    import anthropic
    r = frappe.cache()
    client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=frappe.conf.get("anthropic_api_key", ""))

    resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input=query)
    q_vec = resp.data[0].embedding

    endpoints = frappe.get_all("FB API Endpoint", filters={"is_active": 1}, fields=["name"])
    scores: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
    for ep in endpoints:
        raw = r.get(f"fb:emb:{ep.name}")
        if not raw:
            continue
        e_vec = json.loads(raw)
        # cosine similarity
        dot = sum(a * b for a, b in zip(q_vec, e_vec))
        mag = math.sqrt(sum(a * a for a in q_vec)) * math.sqrt(sum(b * b for b in e_vec))
        scores.append((dot / mag if mag else 0.0, ep.name))

    scores.sort(reverse=True)
    return [{"slug": s, "score": round(sc, 4)} for sc, s in scores[:int(top_k)]]

# ── 19.9  Join path discovery ────────────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def discover_join_paths(primary_doctype: str, target_doctype: str) -> dict:
    """
    Discover how to traverse from primary_doctype to target_doctype via Link fields.
    Returns {paths: [[step, ...], ...], recommended: [step, ...]}.
    """
    def get_links(dt: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        meta = frappe.get_meta(dt)
        return [
            (f.fieldname, f.options)
            for f in meta.fields
            if f.fieldtype == "Link" and f.options
        ]

    # BFS up to depth 3
    visited: set[str] = {primary_doctype}
    queue: list[list[tuple[str, str, str]]] = [[]]  # each element is a path of (from_dt, field, to_dt)
    found_paths: list[list[dict]] = []

    while queue:
        path = queue.pop(0)
        current_dt = path[-1][2] if path else primary_doctype
        if current_dt == target_doctype and path:
            found_paths.append([{"doctype": p[0], "field": p[1], "links_to": p[2]} for p in path])
            continue
        if len(path) >= 3:
            continue
        for field, linked_dt in get_links(current_dt):
            if linked_dt not in visited:
                visited.add(linked_dt)
                queue.append(path + [(current_dt, field, linked_dt)])

    if not found_paths:
        return {"paths": [], "recommended": [], "note": "No path found within depth 3"}

    # Ask AI to recommend best path
    system = "You are a Frappe data model expert."
    prompt = (
        f"Joining {primary_doctype} → {target_doctype}.\n"
        f"Possible paths:\n{json.dumps(found_paths, indent=2)}\n\n"
        "Which path is most semantically meaningful for an API join? "
        "Return JSON: {recommended: [path steps], reason: str}. ONLY JSON."
    )
    reply = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=256)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
    rec = json.loads(m.group()) if m else {}
    return {"paths": found_paths, "recommended": rec.get("recommended", []), "reason": rec.get("reason", "")}


# ── 19.10  custom_logic code generation ──────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def generate_custom_logic(slug: str, requirement: str) -> dict:
    """
    Generate Python custom_logic code for an endpoint given a plain-English requirement.
    Returns {code, explanation}.
    """
    cfg = _load_cfg(slug)
    system = textwrap.dedent("""
        You write FlowBridge custom_logic Python snippets.
        The snippet runs after the main query. Available variables:
          results (list of dicts), cfg (endpoint config), frappe (frappe module),
          request_data (dict of query params / POST body).
        The snippet must reassign `results` if it modifies the list.
        Return a JSON object: {code: "python code string", explanation: "brief str"}.
        Return ONLY valid JSON.
    """)
    prompt = (
        f"Endpoint: {slug} (primary_doctype: {cfg.primary_doctype})\n"
        f"Requirement: {requirement}"
    )
    reply = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=800)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
    result = json.loads(m.group()) if m else {}
    if not result.get("code"):
        # Fallback: treat entire reply as code
        result = {"code": reply, "explanation": ""}
    return result


# ── 19.11  Computed field expression generation ───────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def generate_computed_expression(doctype: str, expression_goal: str) -> dict:
    """
    Generate a Python expression for a computed field given a plain-English goal.
    Returns {expression, example_output, notes}.
    """
    meta = frappe.get_meta(doctype)
    fields_summary = [
        {"fieldname": f.fieldname, "fieldtype": f.fieldtype, "label": f.label}
        for f in meta.fields
        if f.fieldtype not in ("Section Break", "Column Break", "Tab Break")
    ][:40]

    system = "You generate Python expressions for Frappe computed fields in FB API Endpoint configs."
    prompt = (
        f"DocType: {doctype}\n"
        f"Available fields:\n{json.dumps(fields_summary)}\n\n"
        f"Goal: {expression_goal}\n\n"
        "Each row in `results` is a dict. Write a Python expression (not a statement) "
        "that transforms a single row dict `r`. E.g. `r['salary'] * 12`.\n"
        "Return JSON: {expression: str, example_output: str, notes: str}. ONLY JSON."
    )
    reply = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=400)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
    return json.loads(m.group()) if m else {"expression": reply, "example_output": "", "notes": ""}


# ── 19.12  Automated test case generation ────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def generate_test_cases(slug: str) -> dict:
    """
    Generate a pytest test file for the endpoint covering happy path, edge cases,
    and auth/rate-limit boundaries.
    Returns {filename, code}.
    """
    cfg = _load_cfg(slug)
    system = textwrap.dedent("""
        You write pytest integration tests for FlowBridge API endpoints.
        Tests call the endpoint via HTTP using `requests`. Use fixtures for auth headers.
        Cover: happy path GET, pagination, invalid auth (401), rate limit (429),
        POST with valid body, POST with missing required field, PATCH update.
        Return JSON: {filename: str, code: str}. ONLY JSON.
    """)
    prompt = f"Endpoint config:\n{json.dumps(_endpoint_dict(cfg), indent=2)}"
    reply = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=2000)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
    result = json.loads(m.group()) if m else {}
    if not result.get("code"):
        result = {
            "filename": f"test_{slug.replace('-','_')}_ai.py",
            "code": reply,
        }
    return result


# ── 19.13  Postman AI descriptions ───────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def enrich_postman_descriptions(collection_json: str) -> str:
    """
    Given a Postman Collection v2.1 JSON string, enrich each request's description
    with AI-generated prose. Returns the enriched collection JSON string.
    """
    collection: dict = json.loads(collection_json)
    system = "You write concise, developer-friendly descriptions for Postman API requests."

    def _enrich_item(item: dict) -> dict:
        name = item.get("name", "")
        request = item.get("request", {})
        prompt = (
            f"API request name: {name}\n"
            f"Method: {request.get('method','GET')}\n"
            f"URL: {request.get('url', {}).get('raw', '')}\n"
            "Write a 2-sentence description explaining what this request does and "
            "what a developer should know before using it. Plain text only."
        )
        desc = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], max_tokens=120)
        item.setdefault("request", {})["description"] = desc
        return item

    items = collection.get("item", [])
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        if "request" in item:
            items[i] = _enrich_item(item)
        elif "item" in item:  # folder
            for j, sub in enumerate(item["item"]):
                item["item"][j] = _enrich_item(sub)

    return json.dumps(collection, indent=2)


# ── 19.14  Anomaly explanation ────────────────────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def explain_anomaly(slug: str, anomaly_type: str, current_value: Any, baseline_value: Any) -> str:
    """
    Explain a detected usage anomaly in plain English with possible causes and recommendations.
    anomaly_type: 'spike' | 'drop' | 'high_error_rate' | 'slow_latency'
    """
    cfg_fields: dict = {}
    try:
        cfg_fields = _endpoint_dict(_load_cfg(slug))
    except Exception:
        pass

    system = "You are an API observability expert helping developers understand anomalies."
    prompt = (
        f"Endpoint: {slug}\n"
        f"Anomaly type: {anomaly_type}\n"
        f"Current value: {current_value}\n"
        f"Baseline value: {baseline_value}\n"
        f"Endpoint config summary: {json.dumps(cfg_fields)}\n\n"
        "Provide:\n"
        "1. A plain-English explanation of what this anomaly likely means\n"
        "2. 3 probable root causes\n"
        "3. 2 recommended actions to investigate or resolve it\n"
        "Keep the total response under 200 words."
    )
    return _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=350)


# ── 19.15  Zero-result search fix suggestions ────────────────────────────────

@frappe.whitelist()
def suggest_zero_result_fix(slug: str, query_params: str) -> dict:
    """
    When an endpoint returns zero results, suggest likely causes and config fixes.
    query_params: JSON string of the request params that returned nothing.
    Returns {causes: [...], config_patches: [...], example_fix: str}.
    """
    cfg = _load_cfg(slug)
    params: dict = json.loads(query_params) if isinstance(query_params, str) else query_params

    # Gather actual row count for reference
    try:
        total = frappe.db.count(cfg.primary_doctype)
    except Exception:
        total = "unknown"

    system = "You are a FlowBridge API debugging assistant."
    prompt = (
        f"Endpoint: {slug}\n"
        f"Primary doctype: {cfg.primary_doctype} (total rows in DB: {total})\n"
        f"Default filters: {cfg.default_filters}\n"
        f"Request params that returned 0 results: {json.dumps(params)}\n\n"
        "Identify why zero results were returned and how to fix it. "
        "Return JSON: {causes: [str,...], config_patches: [{field,current,suggested},...], example_fix: str}. "
        "ONLY JSON."
    )
    reply = _claude([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], system=system, max_tokens=600)
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", reply, re.DOTALL)
    return json.loads(m.group()) if m else {"causes": [], "config_patches": [], "example_fix": reply}

# FILE: /Users/bluephoenix/frappe-bench/bench-r2/apps/frappe_flowbridge/frappe_flowbridge/flowbridge/api/api_analytics.py
"""
Observability & analytics — Phase 17-C (17.16–17.21).
Per-endpoint stats, slow-query detection, error-rate alerts, dependency map, anomaly detection.
